title: C152 — Front fog lamp LH connector reference
introduction:
I use this page to give the left front fog lamp's electrical connection a clear identity. The housing drawing is the visual landmark, the cavity labels are the addresses, and the pin table explains the connections at those addresses. A plug's silhouette gets you oriented on the page; its labels keep the wiring story straight.

Begin with the identity table, then match each illustrated cavity label to its table row. Read across for circuit identity, wire information, function and terminal reference. The housing Color and the pin table's wire Color describe different items. Keep the lamp's side designation separate from the ground destination named in the Function field; they are not interchangeable location labels.

The pigtail table is a service cross-reference. This page does not teach physical access, viewing direction, probing, diagnosis or replacement. Size and Used remain recorded codes, and Gauge entries retain their original convention without conversion.

edits.why: The broad rectangular top, elongated rounded contact area and small projecting bottom tab distinguish the supplied drawing. I use those features as landmarks, then read the cavity labels directly. The Fpn and Harness Id beneath the illustration associate it with the connector record. These visual details do not establish a viewing side or a tab-release movement.

Cavity connects the drawing to the appropriate row, and Function distinguishes the fog-lamp control connection from the ground return. Circuit Number identifies each circuit; the wire and terminal fields stay with that row. A function describes the recorded electrical role, not a measured result or a reason to condemn the lamp.

A pigtail combines the connector with attached wire leads. I connect Kit List with Number in this table and compare Engineering Shell with Hard Shell in the identity record. Service Part and Image serve different purposes: a service reference and an illustration filename. Keep the pigtail Gauge entry distinct from the individual circuit entries; this table does not establish wire substitutions or installation steps.
